== Setting ==
Works within the ''Neon Genesis Evangelion'' franchise typically have the same setting, characters, and themes, but can vary in their portrayal of the different storylines with alternate re-tellings of the original anime.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dennison |first=Kara |title=VIDEO: All 37 Evangelion Timelines Explained! |url=https://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2019/06/22/video-all-37-evangelion-timelines-explained |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=Crunchyroll |language=en-us |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904225227/https://www.crunchyroll.com/news/latest/2019/6/22/video-all-37-evangelion-timelines-explained |url-status=live }}</ref> Many later works, such as ''Death & Rebirth'' and ''The Rebuild of Evangelion,'' diverge greatly from the original anime.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 3, 2019 |title=Neon Genesis Evangelion Has Some Truly Bizarre Spinoffs |language=en-US |work=CBR |url=https://www.cbr.com/neon-genesis-evangelion-bizarre-spinoffs/ |access-date=February 18, 2023 |archive-date=March 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200319225039/https://www.cbr.com/neon-genesis-evangelion-bizarre-spinoffs/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Evangelion''{{'}}s fictional setting takes place after the Second Impact, a cataclysmic explosion in [[Antarctica]] in the year 2000,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Happy Second Impact! |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2000-09-13/happy-second-impact |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=Anime News Network |language=en |archive-date=November 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191101144234/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2000-09-13/happy-second-impact |url-status=live}}</ref> which killed billions of people and threw the Earth off its axis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=【エヴァ解説】セカンドインパクトとは？原因や意味を初心者でも分かりやすく！ ｜ ドラマスクリーン |url=https://happymackeyblog.com/evangelion-second-impact/ |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=ドラマスクリーン |date=January 11, 2021 |language=ja |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904225736/https://happymackeyblog.com/evangelion-second-impact/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Fifteen years after the Second Impact, a group of mysterious beings referred to as "[[List of Angels in Neon Genesis Evangelion|Angels]]"<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Guide to Angels from Neon Genesis Evangelion [Part 1] |url=https://sabukaru.online/articles/a-guide-to-angels-from-neon-genesis-evangelion-part1 |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=sabukaru |date=March 4, 2021 |language=en-US |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904225736/https://sabukaru.online/articles/a-guide-to-angels-from-neon-genesis-evangelion-part1 |url-status=live }}</ref> begin appearing and pose a worldwide and existential threat to what remains of mankind. The NERV organization, a paramilitary special agency recruited and controlled by the UN, is tasked with defeating the Angels,<ref>{{Cite web |title=NEON GENESIS EVANGELION (20) |url=https://www.animanga.com/scripts/textesgb/eva20.html |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=www.animanga.com |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904225757/https://www.animanga.com/scripts/textesgb/eva20.html |url-status=live }}</ref> with the use of giant mechanical warriors known as "[[Evangelion (mecha)|Evangelions]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=What are EVAs, the Giant Battle Robots of 'Neon Genesis Evangelion'? |url=https://www.thrillist.com/entertainment/nation/neon-genesis-evangelion-what-are-evas-explained |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=Thrillist |date=June 20, 2019 |language=en |archive-date=January 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124082632/https://www.thrillist.com/entertainment/nation/neon-genesis-evangelion-what-are-evas-explained |url-status=live }}</ref> A select group of children pilot the Evangelions, with focus put on [[Shinji Ikari]], [[Rei Ayanami]] and [[Asuka Langley Soryu]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Evangelion Units and Pilots / Neon Genesis Evangelion / Anime - Otapedia {{!}} Tokyo Otaku Mode |url=https://otakumode.com/otapedia/anime/neon_genesis_evangelion/units_pilots |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=otakumode.com |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904225749/https://otakumode.com/otapedia/anime/neon_genesis_evangelion/units_pilots |url-status=live }}</ref> As the story progresses, it delves into [[philosophical]] and [[psychological]] themes such as [[Identity (social science)|identity]], [[Psychological trauma|trauma]], and the [[Existentialism|nature of existence]]. The relationships between the characters are also explored, particularly between Shinji, Asuka, and Rei, as they navigate their complex and sometimes contentious dynamics. The backdrop of ''Neon Genesis Evangelion'' slowly reveals the true nature of Rei Ayanami, the Evangelions, the Angels, the NERV organization and a group known as SEELE.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 20, 2022 |title=What is SEELE in Neon Genesis Evangelion? - Gundam Link |url=https://gundam-link.net/what-is-seele-in-neon-genesis-evangelion/ |access-date=February 17, 2023 |language=en-US |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904230832/https://gundam-link.net/what-is-seele-in-neon-genesis-evangelion/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The series incorporates religious themes, including [[Christianity]] and [[Kabbalah]]<ref name="forward.com">{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2021 |title=Can Kabbalah explain the most mystifying new movie on Amazon? |url=https://forward.com/culture/474063/kabbalah-neon-genesis-evangelion-30-10-rebuild-amazon-anime-eva-streaming/ |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=The Forward |language=en |archive-date=August 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812180935/https://forward.com/culture/474063/kabbalah-neon-genesis-evangelion-30-10-rebuild-amazon-anime-eva-streaming/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Adam]], [[Lilith]] and the [[Dead Sea Scrolls]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=What caused the second impact in NGE?? |url=https://alt.anime.narkive.com/mQCvanNO/what-caused-the-second-impact-in-nge |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=alt.anime.narkive.com |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904232433/https://alt.anime.narkive.com/mQCvanNO/what-caused-the-second-impact-in-nge |url-status=live }}</ref> The series is well known for its [[psychoanalysis]] of the characters and features the theories of famous psychologists like [[Jung]] and [[Freud]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kogod |first=Theo |date=January 27, 2020 |title=Neon Genesis Evangelion: 10 Undeniable Ways That It Changed Mecha Anime Forever |url=https://www.cbr.com/neon-genesis-evangelion-changed-mecha-anime/ |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=CBR |language=en |archive-date=March 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329142737/https://www.cbr.com/neon-genesis-evangelion-changed-mecha-anime/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Fujie |first=Kazuhisa |title=Neon genesis evangelion : the unofficial guide |date=2004 |publisher=DH Pub |others=Martin Foster |isbn=0-9745961-4-0 |location=Tokyo |oclc=56326204}}</ref> This is most heavily covered in the implementation of the Human Instrumentality Project, the secret goal of NERV and SEELE, whose result varies across different media, including the original anime, films, manga and video games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Religion and Symbolism in Neon Genesis Evangelion |url=https://myanimelist.net/featured/1361/Religion_and_Symbolism_in_Neon_Genesis_Evangelion |access-date=January 27, 2023 |website=MyAnimeList.net |language=en |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904232433/https://myanimelist.net/featured/1361/Religion_and_Symbolism_in_Neon_Genesis_Evangelion |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Petit Eva: Evangelion@School'' ===
''Petit Eva: Evangelion@School'' is a [[Chibi (slang)|chibi]]-style [[Original net animation|ONA]] series that ran for 24 broadcasts from March 20, 2007, to March 11,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Petit Eva - Evangelion@School (OAV) - Anime News Network |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/encyclopedia/anime.php?id=8539 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=www.animenewsnetwork.com |archive-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217150921/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/encyclopedia/anime.php?id=8539 |url-status=live }}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=April 2026|reason=User-generated source}} 2009. It was adapted from the ''Petit Eva'' and ''Petit Eva Bokura Tanken Dōkōkai'' spin-off manga illustrated by [[Ryusuke Hamamoto]] and Maki Ozora.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Petit Eva Super-Deformed Series to Be Made into Video |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2007-08-06/petit-eva-super-deformed-series-to-be-made-into-video |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=Anime News Network |language=en |archive-date=May 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525140904/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2007-08-06/petit-eva-super-deformed-series-to-be-made-into-video |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Petit Eva - Baka-Updates Manga |url=https://www.mangaupdates.com/series/lg840pg/petit-eva |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=www.mangaupdates.com |archive-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217150921/https://www.mangaupdates.com/series/lg840pg/petit-eva |url-status=live }}</ref> It is a parody of the original series, where the [[List of Neon Genesis Evangelion characters|original cast]] are now students at a junior high school in Tokyo-3. There are other minor differences to ''Neon Genesis Evangelion'' as well, such as the fact that the three Rei clones are now sisters and that [[Evangelion (mecha)|Evangelion Unit-01]] is now a human-sized student.<ref>{{Citation |title=Petit Eva: Evangelion@School |url=https://myanimelist.net/anime/4130/Petit_Eva__EvangelionSchool |language=en |access-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217150918/https://myanimelist.net/anime/4130/Petit_Eva__EvangelionSchool |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Petit Eva: Evangelion@School / Neon Genesis Evangelion / Anime - Otapedia {{!}} Tokyo Otaku Mode |url=https://otakumode.com/otapedia/anime/neon_genesis_evangelion/petit_eva |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=otakumode.com |archive-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217150918/https://otakumode.com/otapedia/anime/neon_genesis_evangelion/petit_eva |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Manga and light novel ==
{{main|Neon Genesis Evangelion (manga){{!}}''Neon Genesis Evangelion'' (manga)}}A number of [[manga]] series based on the anime have been released, most notably the [[Neon Genesis Evangelion (manga)|official series]] by series character designer [[Yoshiyuki Sadamoto]], which was first serialized in February 1995 (eight months before the series' official premiere, in order to promote interest), and ended in November 2014, 19 years later. Seven other manga have been created: the shoujo romance story ''[[Neon Genesis Evangelion: Angelic Days]]'' by [[Fumino Hayashi]], shonen comedy ''[[Shinji Ikari Raising Project]]'' by Takahashi Osamu, self-parody ''[[List of Neon Genesis Evangelion chapters#It's A Miraculous Win|It's A Miraculous Win]]'' by Koume Yoshida, mystery series ''[[Neon Genesis Evangelion: Campus Apocalypse]]'' by Min Min, [[Chibi (slang)|''chibi'']] comedic parody ''[[List of Neon Genesis Evangelion chapters#Petit Eva: Evangelion@School|Petit Eva: Evangelion@School]]'', detective story ''[[List of Neon Genesis Evangelion chapters#Neon Genesis Evangelion: The Shinji Ikari Detective Diary|Neon Genesis Evangelion: The Shinji Ikari Detective Diary]]'' and [[gamer]]-themed parody ''[[List of Neon Genesis Evangelion chapters#Neon Genesis Evangelion: Legend of the Piko-Piko Middle School Students|Neon Genesis Evangelion: Legend of the Piko-Piko Middle School Students]].''

A [[light novel]] series ''[[Neon Genesis Evangelion: ANIMA]]'' was serialized from 2008 to 2013 in Dengeki Hobby Magazine, authored by the series mechanical designer [[Ikuto Yamashita]]. The series is set in an alternate future diverging from the events of the anime. The novel begins 3 years after the end of the Human Instrumentality Project, replacing episodes 25 and 26 of the anime, as well as the End of Evangelion film. The team of former Eva pilots are coming to terms with the aftermath of the battle at NERV HQ, while adapting to normal life. Three clones of Rei Ayanami have been put into Eva units and sent into space as a precautionary way to seek out and eradicate the remaining mass-produced Evangelion units, as well as monitor Earth's safety. In 2021, the final film of the [[Rebuild of Evangelion|''Rebuild of Evangelion'']] tetralogy, ''[[Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time]],'' received a re-release dubbed ''3.0+1.01'' that included a prequel manga to the events of ''[[Evangelion: 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo]]'' titled ''[[List of Neon Genesis Evangelion chapters#Evangelion 3.0 (-120 min.)|Evangelion 3.0 (-120 min.)]]'', written by co-director [[Kazuya Tsurumaki]] at Hideaki Anno's initiative.<ref>{{Cite web|date=June 7, 2021|title=6月12日(土)より『シン・エヴァンゲリオン劇場版』ラストラン、感謝を込めて3つの大サービス！|url=https://www.evangelion.co.jp/news/210607-2/|url-status=live|access-date=August 17, 2021|website=www.evangelion.co.jp|language=ja|archive-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227063836/https://www.evangelion.co.jp/news/210607-2/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=July 9, 2021|title=15年ぶりの漫画で、見たことのない「エヴァ」を描く／「シン・エヴァンゲリオン劇場版」特典冊子を描く監督・前田真宏インタビュー|url=https://webnewtype.com/report/article/1041222/|url-status=live|access-date=August 17, 2021|website=WebNewtype|language=ja|archive-date=August 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814051513/https://webnewtype.com/report/article/1041222/}}</ref> It was later adapted in [[motion comic]] form for ''3.0+1.0''<nowiki/>'s home media release.<ref name=":1" />

Vision]] in September 2009 raised concerns over the project's viability, Greenfield, Ledford,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.evageeks.org/2011/06/sunday-supanova-wrap-up/ |title=Sunday Supanova Wrap Up |publisher=EvaGeeks.org |date=June 19, 2011 |access-date=November 21, 2012 |archive-date=October 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008004729/http://www.evageeks.org/2011/06/sunday-supanova-wrap-up/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mediafire.com/?lzxrxuh30y646cj |title=Tiffany Grant & Matt Greenfield Sunday Supanova 2011.MP3 |publisher=Mediafire.com |access-date=November 21, 2012 |archive-date=November 6, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106063604/http://www.evageeks.org/2011/06/sunday-supanova-wrap-up/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and producer Joseph Chou<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2010-02-04/producer/live-action-evangelion-project-still-active|title=Producer: Live-Action Evangelion Project Still Active|publisher=Anime News Network|date=February 4, 2010|access-date=August 13, 2011|archive-date=August 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826191811/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2010-02-04/producer/live-action-evangelion-project-still-active|url-status=live}}</ref> insisted the project was still actively searching for a director.

In August 2011, A.D. Vision sued Gainax, claiming their refusal to accept an [[Option (filmmaking)|option]] payment for the perpetual live-action rights to ''Evangelion'' was a breach of contract and resulted in losing an opportunity to produce the film with a major studio. ADV had asked to be awarded the full live-action rights and any accruing [[English rule (attorney's fees)|legal fees]]. It was one of multiple legal battles between Gainax and ADV. Gainax rejected this claim and returned their payment of $100,000.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lanson |first=Greg |date=August 12, 2011 |title=A.D. Vision, Inc. sues Gainax Co., Ltd. over live-action Evangelion movie agreement |url=http://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2011/08/12/ad-vision-inc-sues-gainax-co-ltd-over-live-action-evangelion-movie-agreement |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110920193657/http://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2011/08/12/ad-vision-inc-sues-gainax-co-ltd-over-live-action-evangelion-movie-agreement |archive-date=September 20, 2011 |access-date=August 13, 2011 |publisher=Crunchyroll}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Loo |first=Egan |date=August 12, 2011 |title=ADV Sues Gainax Over Live-Action Evangelion Option (Updated) |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2011-08-12/adv-sues-gainax-over-live-action-evangelion-option |access-date=September 4, 2023 |website=Anime News Network |language=en |archive-date=December 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220060824/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2011-08-12/adv-sues-gainax-over-live-action-evangelion-option |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Tiffany Grant]], voice actress for Asuka in the ADV localization and then married to Greenfield, told [[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] in 2019 that the project was a dud and never had a shooting script or any signed crew or cast.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Covill |first=Max |date=June 26, 2019 |title=What happened to the Neon Genesis Evangelion live-action movie |url=https://www.polygon.com/2019/6/26/18758581/neon-genesis-evangelion-movie-live-action-netflix-anime |access-date=September 4, 2023 |website=Polygon |language=en-US |archive-date=June 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626160111/https://www.polygon.com/2019/6/26/18758581/neon-genesis-evangelion-movie-live-action-netflix-anime |url-status=live }}</ref> Although Weta artists had talked with some Gainax staff, by that time Anno had already set on making the ''Rebuild'' films, and had started to take the franchise with him to his new studio Khara, despite ADV continuing to negotiate only with Gainax, and the project faded into abandonment.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gdnYPmd0lgs |title=Interview With Weta Regarding: Live Action Evangelion Movie |date=March 6, 2006 |type=Video |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

Anno has been questioned on a live-action adaptation of ''Evangelion'', particularly a Western one, multiple times. He has shown himself resistant to the idea. Anno reiterated that ''Eva'' was always conceived as an animation and made with a Japanese audience with mind, and he believes Western creators have too different a mindset and methods compared to Japanese creators: "There may be Japanese film-makers who can collaborate with Western creators, but I'm not one of them".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shackleton |first=Liz |date=December 19, 2014 |title=Hideaki Anno, Evangelion |url=https://www.screendaily.com/awards/hideaki-anno-evangelion/5081255.article |access-date=September 4, 2023 |website=ScreenDaily |language=en |archive-date=September 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904233011/https://www.screendaily.com/awards/hideaki-anno-evangelion/5081255.article |url-status=live }}</ref> He also dislikes live-action adaptations of anime, as well as live-action works inspired by anime overall. Anno believes ''Eva'' could not be properly expressed in live-action, and strongly dislikes the idea of Hollywood remaking it.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schilling |first=Mark |date=October 18, 2014 |title=Hideaki Anno: emotional deconstructionist |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/2014/10/18/films/hideaki-anno-emotional-deconstructionist/ |access-date=September 4, 2023 |website=The Japan Times |language=en |archive-date=October 19, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019152156/https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/2014/10/18/films/hideaki-anno-emotional-deconstructionist/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Other media ==
The ''Evangelion'' franchise has spread from the original anime into a number of different media, with some following the official [[Canon (fiction)|canon]] (of the 26-episode anime series and its three related films or the new ''Rebuild'' series) and others differing on important plot points originally introduced in the anime.

Neon Genesis Evangelion (新世紀エヴァンゲリオン, Shin Seiki Evangerion; IPA: [ɕin seː.ki e.βaŋ.ge.ɾi.oɴ]) is a Japanese media franchise created by Hideaki Anno, originally owned by Gainax and currently owned by Khara. Most of the franchise features an apocalyptic mecha action story, which revolves around the paramilitary organization NERV and their efforts in fighting hostile beings called Angels, using giant humanoids called Evangelions (or EVAs for short) that are piloted by select teenagers. Subsequent works deviate from this theme to varying degrees, focusing more on romantic interactions between the characters, plotlines not present in the original works, and reimaginings of the conflicts from the original works.
The Neon Genesis Evangelion manga debuted in Shōnen Ace in December 1994, to generate interest in the upcoming anime release. The Neon Genesis Evangelion anime was written and directed by Hideaki Anno, originally airing from October 1995 until March 1996. The anime is widely considered to have been groundbreaking in its exploration of religious, psychological, and philosophical themes, while initially appearing to be a standard mecha series. The ending of the series was controversial; in response to this controversy, two films offered an alternate ending for the show: Neon Genesis Evangelion: Death & Rebirth, released in March 1997, and The End of Evangelion released in July 1997. Death is a 60-minute compilation of parts from the first 24 episodes of the TV series, with some new footage added in order to prepare for Rebirth, which contains the last two episodes and the first 30 minutes of End of Evangelion.
The popularity of the show spawned numerous additional media, including video games, radio dramas, audio books, a light novel series, pachinko machines, and a tetralogy of films titled Rebuild of Evangelion. Other derivative works include Angelic Days, Petit Eva: Evangelion@School and Shinji Ikari Raising Project.
